translation.notTranslated: This page has not yet been translated into {lang}. The original text is shown below.
translation.machineWarning: This translation was produced by machine translation and has not yet been reviewed by a human.
translation.outdated: The original text was updated; this translation is being reviewed.

peoples.originMapNote: The red point is the hypothesized ancient homeland of the Turkic peoples (a scholarly theory, not an established fact). Blue points are each people's main present-day location. The connecting lines are schematic and do not represent an exact historical migration route.
peoples.statusYoq: No state entity of its own
peoples.statNone: No state entity of their own
peoples.estimateNote: There is no single scholarly confirmed estimate — this range comes from popular reference works and needs verification.
peoples.worldShareNote: Calculated from the range above and world population ({world}, {year}, UN).
peoples.populationChartNote: Only the figure for the main country of each people; years and sources differ and diasporas are excluded — so these numbers cannot be added up into a total.
peoples.legendCountryTotal: Total population of the country — not an ethnic count
peoples.legendEstimate: Approximate figure whose source needs re-checking

states.territoryMapNote: This is not a border — it is a schematic shape illustrating the general extent described in the text, roughly corresponding to the state's period of greatest expansion.
states.territoryPopup: Approximate, schematic extent — not a precise historical border.
states.tableCaption: Text alternative for the map data
states.mapDisclaimer: Borders are approximate and schematic — this is a draft not yet fully reviewed by an expert.
states.mapAriaLabel: Map of the approximate extent of {title}
states.symbolsNote: Schematic redrawing based on the description in the source — not a photograph of an original object.
states.symbolsPending: Symbols of this state are recorded in sources, but they are not drawn here until an expert confirms their exact form.
states.symbolsNone: No reliable source has yet been found for a symbol (standard, tamga or flag) of this state. "Historical flag" images found online are usually modern interpretations.
states.sortedNote: States are ordered by founding year. The category badge shows how each state relates to the Turkic world.
states.centuryChartNote: States that existed for at least part of the century are counted. Some dates are approximate, so the figures show the general picture.
states.timelineNote: Each bar shows the period a state existed. Bars with faded ends have approximate dates. Click a bar to open the state's page.
states.capitalsMapNote: Each dot is the capital of at least one state (in different periods); these are not historical borders. A numbered dot is a city that served as capital of several states. Hover over a dot to see the list of states.

topics.capitalsMapNote: The map only shows the geographic location of capital cities — it is not a depiction of historical borders.
